### **Job Description and Duties**

The Continuous Environmental Monitoring (CEM) unit maintains a network of water quality stations throughout the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta. This position offers an exciting opportunity to join our interdisciplinary team of environmental scientists, engineers, technicians, and other specialists while contributing to a dynamic field program and supporting high-quality science focused on the restoration, conservation, and management of the San Francisco Estuary.

  

This position plays an integral role in supporting program operations through the collection, analysis, management, and reporting of environmental data to ensure regulatory compliance with Water Right Decision 1641. Responsibilities include operating and maintaining water quality monitoring equipment and station infrastructure, collecting and processing environmental samples, evaluating data quality, and managing long-term environmental data sets. The incumbent will also contribute to technical reports and presentations and participate in special studies addressing emerging water quality issues in the Bay-Delta. This position also provides opportunities to work collaboratively with scientists and other specialists within and outside of DWR to help inform the management and protection of the San Francisco Estuary. You will find additional information about the position in the Duty Statement.

  

**As a permanent-intermittent position, the incumbent may not exceed working 1,500 hours in a calendar year. Permanent-intermittent (PI) employees are eligible to receive benefits after meeting the required work hour criteria and do receive holiday pay on a pro-rated basis.**

  

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

jobs.title: Water Resources Planner / Scientist
jobs.description:
**About Us**  
  
We are an award-winning California-based environmental consulting firm with 600+ professionals and more than 30 years of diverse experience serving clients in transportation, energy, water, infrastructure, private development, and government sectors. Our mission is to deliver practical, science-based environmental and planning solutions that support communities, infrastructure, and natural systems.  
  
As a people-centric organization, we value collaboration, fairness, and transparency, and are committed to fostering a workplace that supports both personal and professional growth while offering robust career opportunities. We are especially proud of our recent **Great Place To Work®**certification, which reflects an independent assessment of our culture and our team-member experiences.  
  
**About The Role**  
  
Rincon is seeking a **Water Resources Planner/Scientist** with a background in California water supply/reliability, Sustainable Groundwater Management Act (SGMA), geology, hydrology, or hydrogeology to support our growing groundwater and water resources practice across California. This role will focus primarily on SGMA planning and implementation, watershed resilience planning, nature-based and groundwater recharge solutions, water resources planning, and grant funding strategies that move water resource solutions from planning toward implementation. Working with Project Managers, Principals-in-Charge, and interdisciplinary technical teams, you will conduct technical research and analysis; analyze groundwater, hydrologic, water quality, and other water resource data; and contribute to technical reports, planning documents, and funding applications. You will also work with public agency clients and interested parties throughout the planning process, helping to gather and evaluate data, support technical analyses, and communicate findings and recommendations. You will have opportunities to build the technical experience needed for greater responsibility and professional growth.  
  
You will interact with public agency clients, contribute to community outreach and engagement, and help strengthen client relationships through high-quality project delivery.  
  
We are looking for a motivated, curious, and collaborative professional who is eager to learn and make a tangible impact. This is an opportunity to build technical expertise, work alongside experienced water resources professionals, and help shape the next generation of sustainable and resilient water management across California.  
  
**How We Collaborate**  
  
This role may offer a hybrid work setup, blending time in the office with remote work as business needs evolve. We enjoy coming together in person to collaborate, connect with teammates, and partner with clients, and may prioritize candidates who live within 50 miles of a Rincon office.

Eligible office locations for this role include **Carlsbad, Fresno, Los Angeles, Monterey, Oakland, Palm Springs, Riverside, Sacramento, San Luis Obispo, San Diego, San Jose, Santa Barbara, and Ventura.**  
  
**What You’ll Do**

* Support SGMA planning and implementation, including Groundwater Sustainability Plans and Alternatives, annual reports, periodic evaluations, plan updates, groundwater monitoring and data analysis, and evaluation of projects and management actions.
* Contribute to watershed resilience and climate adaptation planning by evaluating groundwater and surface water conditions, hydrology, water supply reliability, drought and climate impacts, and opportunities to improve long-term watershed resilience.
* Evaluate nature-based and groundwater sustainability solutions, including managed aquifer recharge, groundwater recharge, habitat and watershed restoration, stormwater capture, and green infrastructure, using geologic, hydrologic, hydrogeologic, and other technical information.
* Support grant applications and funding strategies for groundwater sustainability, recharge, watershed resilience, water supply, recycled water, wastewater, stormwater, and other water resource projects, including evaluating project benefits, readiness, and alignment with funding opportunities.
* Contribute to complex water resources planning documents, including Urban Water Management Plans, Water Shortage Contingency Plans, water supply and recycled water feasibility studies, watershed management plans, technical memoranda, and permitting and funding applications for water/wastewater facilities.
* Conduct technical research, field investigations, and analysis of groundwater, surface water, water supply, water quality, and related geologic and hydrologic conditions to support water resource planning, permitting, and project implementation.
* Prepare materials to support community and governing body engagement related to water resources projects, including drafting e-blasts, social media posts, presentations, resolutions and staff reports, posters, interview/input questions, surveys, and summaries of engagement efforts.
* Analyze and interpret technical data, including groundwater levels, water quality, water use, hydrologic conditions, and other datasets, and translate findings into clear, client-ready technical conclusions and recommendations.
* Prepare technical memoranda, reports, planning documents, presentations, and other materials for public agency clients and interested parties.
* Work collaboratively with hydrogeologists, geologists, engineers, planners, biologists, and other technical specialists and support client and stakeholder meetings, outreach, and project delivery.

**What You’ll Bring**

* Bachelor’s degree in Geology, Hydrogeology, Hydrology, Water Resources, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, or a related technical field.
* Two or more years of relevant professional experience in groundwater, water resources, watershed management, hydrology, environmental planning, or a related field with an emphasis on SGMA and watershed resiliency.

jobs.title: Senior Air Quality Consultant
jobs.description:
Position Summary:

We are seeking a highly skilled and experienced Senior Air Quality Consultant to join our team. The ideal candidate will have extensive experience with the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and regulatory compliance (reporting and permitting). This role involves managing complex air quality projects, ensuring compliance with environmental regulations, and providing expert guidance to clients.

Responsibilities:  

* Lead and manage air quality assessments and impact analyses for various projects.
* Ensure compliance with CEQA and other relevant environmental regulations.
* Prepare and review technical reports, including air quality impact assessments and mitigation plans.
* Conduct air quality modeling and data analysis.
* Provide expert advice and support to clients on air quality issues and regulatory requirements.
* Complete air quality permits under SCAQMD, SJVAPCD, BAAQMD and other Air Districts, including Title V Permits
* Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to develop and implement air quality management strategies.
* Stay updated on the latest developments in air quality regulations and best practices.
* Mentor and train junior staff members.

Requirements:

* Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, or a related field.
* Minimum of 10 years of experience in air quality consulting, with a focus on CEQA and regulatory compliance.
* Strong knowledge of air quality regulations, including CEQA, the Clean Air Act, and local air district rules.
* Proficiency in air quality modeling software (e.g., AERMOD, CalEEMod).
* Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and project management skills.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
* Professional certifications (e.g., CPP, QEP, PE) are a plus.

The pay range for this California position is $120,000- $170,000 per year; however, base pay offered may be higher or lower depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience of the candidate.

Benefits:

NV5

NV5 offers a competitive compensation and benefits package including medical, dental, life insurance, PTO, 401(k) and professional development/advancement opportunities.

  

* Competitive Salary
* Medical, dental, and supplemental insurance
* Employee Assistance Program
* Company paid Life & AD&D
* Company paid Disability
* 401K Plan
* Paid Holidays
* Paid Time Off

  
Company Overview:

NV5

NV5 delivers technology-enabled engineering, consulting, and geospatial solutions that help clients plan, design, and optimize infrastructure, buildings, utilities, and environmental systems. We bring together technical expertise, data, and innovative thinking to create resilient, high-performance assets. As part of TiC Solutions, alongside Acuren, we share a purpose: **to shape and strengthen the physical world.**

Our work starts with our people. We invest in their growth and never compromise on safety. We work as **one team** across disciplines and geographies, bringing diverse perspectives and a shared purpose to complex challenges.

At NV5, we take pride in high-quality work that creates lasting value for our clients. We challenge the status quo, continuously improve, and turn insight into smarter designs, plans, and solutions. Join us to contribute your expertise and collaborate with our teams to help shape the infrastructure and systems the world relies on.

jobs.title: Groundwater & Water Resources Project Manager
jobs.description:
**About Us**  
  
We are an award-winning California-based environmental consulting firm with 600+ professionals and more than 30 years of diverse experience serving clients in transportation, energy, water, infrastructure, private development, and government sectors. Our mission is to deliver practical, science-based environmental and planning solutions that support communities, infrastructure, and natural systems.  
  
As a people-centric organization, we value collaboration, fairness, and transparency, and are committed to fostering a workplace that supports both personal and professional growth while offering robust career opportunities. We are especially proud of our recent **Great Place To Work®**certification, which reflects an independent assessment of our culture and our team-member experiences.  
  
**About The Role**  
  
Rincon is seeking an experienced **Project Manager, Groundwater & Water Resources** to help lead our growing groundwater and water resources practice across California. We are especially interested in candidates who combine strong groundwater and water resources expertise with demonstrated project management and client leadership. California professional licensure, including California Professional Geologist (PG), Certified Engineering Geologist (CEG), or Certified Hydrogeologist (CHG) is preferred for candidates whose background is centered in geology or environmental engineering.  
  
This role will focus primarily on Sustainable Groundwater Management Act (SGMA) planning and implementation, watershed resilience, nature-based and groundwater recharge solutions, water resources planning, and grant funding strategies that move water resource solutions from planning through implementation. The successful candidate will combine technical expertise with strong project management and client leadership skills, working alongside groundwater modelers, hydrologists, engineers, planners, environmental scientists, and other specialists.  
  
This position is well suited for a technical professional ready to take greater ownership of projects and client relationships while continuing to deepen their expertise in groundwater sustainability and integrated water resources management.

**How We Collaborate**  
  
This role may offer a hybrid work setup, blending time in the office with remote work as business needs evolve. We enjoy coming together in person to collaborate, connect with teammates, and partner with clients, and may prioritize candidates who live within 50 miles of a Rincon office.  
  
Eligible office locations for this role include **Carlsbad, Fresno, Los Angeles, Monterey, Oakland, Palm Springs, Riverside, Sacramento, San Luis Obispo, San Diego, San Jose, Santa Barbara, and Ventura.**  
  
**What You’ll Do**

* Lead and manage SGMA planning and implementation, including Groundwater Sustainability Plans (GSPs) and Alternatives, annual reports, periodic evaluations, monitoring programs, evaluation of sustainable management criteria, groundwater projects and management actions, and adaptive management strategies.
* Evaluate complex groundwater and water resource conditions using hydrogeologic, hydrologic, water quality, land use, and climate information, including groundwater levels and storage, water budgets, groundwater-surface water interactions, groundwater dependent ecosystems, and basin sustainability issues.
* Lead or support watershed resilience and climate adaptation efforts, integrating groundwater, surface water, water supply, land use, climate vulnerability, and other technical information to develop practical long-term resilience strategies.
* Evaluate and advance nature-based and groundwater sustainability solutions, including managed aquifer recharge, groundwater recharge, stormwater capture, watershed restoration, green infrastructure, and related water infrastructure, working with multidisciplinary technical teams to assess feasibility, benefits, constraints, and implementation considerations.
* Lead development of grant applications and funding strategies for groundwater sustainability, watershed resilience, recharge, water supply, and other water resource projects, helping clients align technically sound projects with available funding and move priority projects toward implementation.
* Direct and integrate technical work performed by multidisciplinary teams, including groundwater modelers, hydrologists, engineers, geologists, environmental scientists, GIS professionals, and other specialists; review technical analyses and work products for quality, consistency, and defensibility.
* Lead development and QA/QC of complex, multidisciplinary water resources planning documents, including Urban Water Management Plans, Water Shortage Contingency Plans, water supply and recycled water feasibility studies, watershed management plans, technical memoranda, and funding applications.
* Lead development of water supply and demand forecasting models using excel-based decision-support tools, addressing water demand factors, passive and active conservation savings, climate change impacts on water use and supply availability, wastewater and return flow generation, and recycled water/non-potable connections.
* Manage projects and client relationships, including scopes, budgets, schedules, contracts, subcontractors, deliverables, meetings, and multidisciplinary project teams across multiple concurrent assignments.
* Lead planning and facilitation of community and governing body engagement related to water resources projects, including e-blasts, social media posts, presentations, resolutions and staff reports, posters, interview/input sessions, surveys, and summaries of engagement efforts.
* Communicate complex technical information clearly through technical reports and memoranda, presentations, workshops, public meetings, and discussions with Groundwater Sustainability Agencies, water districts, municipalities, state agencies, stakeholders, and other clients.

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
EHS Support is a specialty environmental consulting firm that provides solutions to complex environmental, health, and safety challenges across a range of market sectors and industries. With experts located throughout the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, and South Africa, we form long-lasting partnerships with our clients through a culture of excellence, innovation, work ethic, and integrity. We focus on hiring and retaining talented, motivated people who enjoy collaborating with and delivering value to our clients. Our team does more than identify problems— we provide solutions.

**Location:** Remote (Western Australia)

**Description:** The successful candidate for this position will provide technical support to a diverse range of projects in service areas that include environmental site assessments, remediation, management system development, compliance and sustainability. This will involve work for clients across multiple sectors, including oil and gas, chemical and heavy industry, water resources and others.

The position is primarily a home-office-based position, with periodic fieldwork required. This may involve extended (e.g. two-week trips) to regional areas of Australia. Project work is primarily based in Australia, but there may be opportunities to support projects in the United States and other international locations. The preferred location for this position is Perth/Fremantle, Western Australia, although other locations will be considered.

**Typical responsibilities will include:**

* Management, analysis and presentation of environmental investigation, monitoring and remediation operations data, including groundwater, surface water, soil, recovery and other types of data
* Desktop data gathering and compilation
* Background reviews of technical guidance, regulations and case studies
* Assistance with reporting and preparation of other written deliverables, including: monitoring reports, environmental site assessments, work plans, health and safety plans, proposals, estimated rehabilitation costing, plan of operations, and annual returns
* Implementation of environmental field inspection and monitoring programs, including groundwater and surface water monitoring and soil sampling
* Supervision of subcontractors in the field (e.g. drilling supervision, excavation supervision)
* Project and task management – planning and implementation of scope, schedule, budgets

**Position Requirements:**

This opportunity is for an adaptable, self-motivated individual who desires to gain experience and professional growth across a diverse range of projects. Traits required for success in our team include:

* Critical thinking and analytical skills, with an attention to detail
* Effective technical writing and oral presentation skills
* Ability to think strategically and conceptually and translate strategy into practical and tactical plans
* Ability to work independently, whilst seeking support from other practitioners at key points
* Ability to develop and maintain positive relationships with co-workers and internal clients
* Appreciation and conscientious application of health, safety and environment standards.

**Qualifications for this role include:**

* Bachelor or Masters degree in soil science, hydrogeology, geology, environmental science, environmental engineering or other relevant science/engineering degree.
* Three to five years of experience in a relevant environmental role, including training and experience in groundwater and soil sampling.
* A well-developed understanding of environmental and resource regulations (with a focus on W.A. preferred).
* Advanced user of Microsoft Excel (experience with Power BI and other database management experience is preferred, but not essential)
* Australian experience and a current ability to work in Australia (citizenship or valid visa) is required
* Current Australian state driving license preferred.

jobs.title: Principal Environmental Scientist - Environmental Approvals and Compliance
jobs.description:
**Location:** Remote (Brisbane)

**Summary**

EHS Support is seeking and environmental professional with 15+ years of experience in Queensland and Commonwealth resource approvals and compliance to help us deliver a range of approvals and compliance support to clients.

**Who We Are**

EHS Support is a global team of engineers, scientists and technical professionals who specialise in complex environmental challenges across a wide array of industries and service areas. As innovative professionals in our fields, we challenge conventions and strive to find more efficient and effective approaches to environmental compliance and management. We’re problem solvers and we’re passionate about what we do.

**Why We Are**

EHS Support was founded back in 2005 because we wanted to create a different kind of company — one that was focused on providing solutions through long-term relationships and by treating both clients and employees with an unmatched level of respect. We wanted to solve complex technical problems through entrepreneurial concepts and unconventional ideas. We wanted to provide clients with unequalled service and expertise. Last but not least, we wanted to help our employees grow and thrive in their careers. In essence, we wanted to provide value — value to our employees in the form of opportunity and security, and value to our clients in the form of practical, effective, long-term solutions.

**What We Do**

We partner with our clients to develop technical solutions that address their unique business challenges. Some of our key service areas include contaminated land site assessment and remediation, hydrogeological assessment and services, expert witness and litigation support, risk assessment and toxicology, sediment assessment and remediation, and liability cost estimation and assurance.

**About Our Team**

EHS Support has diversity of experts in the fields of engineering, geology, chemistry, toxicology, risk assessment, finance and others. We have a global presence, with teams based in the U.S., Canada, New Zealand, U.K., South Africa and Australia (including offices in Victoria, Queensland, South Australia and Western Australia).

EHS Support is looking for a Principal Environmental Scientist to join our Australian Approvals and Compliance team. In this role, you will work closely with colleagues from both EHS Support and AES (an integrated EHS Support company) to deliver approvals and compliance projects nationwide, whilst serving as a focal point for Queensland-based clients and projects. Projects will be focused on the resources sector, but there will also be opportunities to work in the development and sustainable energy sectors. This role has a strong business development component and offers the opportunity to grow and lead a Queensland-based approvals and compliance team, leveraging national expertise to deliver projects. You will also work closely with senior leadership to help realise our vision of being recognised as a top-tier provider of primary and secondary approvals. The work activities will be primarily office-based, although occasional travel for field-based work may be required. This position may also present opportunities to contribute to EHS Support’s developing business in decarbonisation/carbon transition, ESG and environmental offsets.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Develop technical proposals and strengthen client relationships through business development.
* Develop new lines of service delivery leveraging your complementary skills and expertise with the national EHS Support/AES team.
* Assist in capacity-building and development of a high performing national compliance and approvals team.
* Lead environmental impact assessments and complex approvals processes.
* Manage projects within scope, budget, and quality standards.
* Mentor junior and mid-level consultants to build their expertise in environmental approvals and compliance.
* Foster collaboration within AES and EHS Supports multidisciplinary teams to deliver exceptional results.

**Key Requirements**

* A degree in a science, engineering or legal discipline
* 15+ years of experience in Queensland and Commonwealth environmental approvals (both primary and secondary approvals)
* Strong understanding of Commonwealth and State environmental legislation.
* Proven ability to build and sustain client relationships.
* Experience within resources sectors preferred.
* Strong written, verbal, and strategic thinking skills.
* Great eye for detail, a sense of practicality in regard to legislative and technical interpretation, and the ability to find pragmatic solutions.
* Authorisation to work in Australia (applications are open to Australian and New Zealand Citizens and Australian Permanent Residents)

  
EHS Support is focused on creating a work environment in which everyone is included, accepted, respected and treated fairly. We are an equal opportunity employer and recognise that diversity includes gender, age, race, disability status, sexual orientation, religion, neurodiversity, education levels, and many more aspects of your identity.

jobs.title: Principal / Senior Principal Environmental Scientist (Contaminated Land)

You will work closely with senior leaders across the Australian and international business to drive growth in Queensland and nationally. While business development and client leadership are central to the role, this position also maintains a hands-on technical component, supported by an established team of experienced professionals. This role offers a clear pathway to equity/shareholding, along with genuine autonomy to shape your portfolio, team and regional growth strategy. We welcome applications from both individual leaders and established teams seeking a new platform to grow. With strong market demand and projected growth, this role provides the opportunity to help shape the future direction of our company.

**What You'll Do:**

In this role, you will combine business development leadership with hands-on technical delivery, supported by an established team of experienced practitioners.

**Key responsibilities include:**

* Originate and secure new work through a proven seller-doer approach, driving revenue growth and market expansion
* Lead and grow client relationships across industrial, government and resources sectors
* Lead and deliver complex contaminated land projects, including high-risk, high-profile technical engagements such as auditing and expert witness work
* Provide strategic environmental advice on regulatory policy, compliance frameworks, assurance and remediation strategy
* Mentor, develop and lead high-performing multidisciplinary teams, fostering accountability, collaboration and technical excellence

**About you**

You are a commercially astute environmental professional with technical credibility and a strong market reputation. You are comfortable operating at both strategic and delivery levels and thrive in roles where growth, leadership and technical excellence intersect.

* Approximately 20–25 years’ experience in environmental consulting, with a strong focus on contaminated land
* Demonstrated seller-doer success, with measurable business development and revenue growth outcomes
* Recognized leadership capability, including delegation, team development and practice growth
* Technical expertise across contaminated land remediation, regulatory compliance, EMS and environmental assurance
* Strong client engagement skills and the ability to operate as a trusted advisor
* A collaborative, entrepreneurial mindset with a genuine interest in shaping culture and long-term business growth

**Compensation and Incentives**

A highly competitive and flexible remuneration structure will be offered, tailored to experience and growth contribution. In addition to base salary and superannuation, this will include:

* Annual performance bonus
* Signing and retention incentives
* Revenue share arrangements
* “Growth Accelerator” bonus linked directly to practice or client base expansion
* Clear, fast-track pathway to equity/shareholding in the global EHS Support business

**Professional growth and support**

We provide practical support and incentives aligned with long-term leadership and growth, including:

* Paid professional memberships (EIANZ, ALGA, Engineers Australia)
* Training & development allowances
* Clear equity/shareholding path

**Bring-Your-Team Option:** We welcome applications from established leaders seeking to transition with staff and clients. Financial incentives and/or additional equity may be available for team-based moves.

**Why EHS Support**

This is more than a senior consulting role — it is a leadership platform. You will have:

* The autonomy to grow your own portfolio and team, supported by established national and global business infrastructure
* A seat at the table in shaping company strategy and regional growth.
* Opportunities to work on complex, high-profile projects across Australia and internationally
* A collaborative, entrepreneurial culture that values ownership, initiative and long-term sustainability

EHS Support is a growing international consultancy with ambitious plans. This role offers a rare opportunity to directly influence both business growth and organizational culture while mentoring the next generation of environmental leaders.
